2026-09-22T10:02:38.0932959Z 
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0934337Z **Trust successful tool responses.** Safeoutputs records write transactions that are applied after the agent finishes. A successful safe-output tool call means the transaction was accepted for downstream application. Do NOT independently verify the effect via `gh`, `gh api`, or other GitHub read paths from the current sandbox, because those paths will not reflect future safe-output writes.

Pattern: /^#?aw_[A-Za-z0-9_]{3,12}$/i (the '#' prefix is optional; bare 'aw_abc1' is accepted and normalised to '#aw_abc1' automatically). Use this form for all field values (temporary_id, item_number, issue_number, parent, etc.). In body/markdown text, '#aw_abc1' references are replaced with the real issue/PR number after creation. 2026-09-22T10:02:38.0975747Z 
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0976596Z For multiple or complex arguments, pipe a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel:
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0977128Z ```bash
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0977520Z printf '{"item_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody."}' | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0978095Z # or write to a file: safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0978519Z ```
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0978652Z 
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0982693Z **Multi-line or long `body` content:** do NOT build the JSON payload with `printf`/`echo` embedding raw newlines or many escaped characters directly in the command line — the sandbox's shell command-injection guard may reject long or complex quoted arguments (reporting "expansion patterns"/"command substitution" even though none are present) and retrying the identical command will fail again. Instead, write the content to a temp file with a heredoc, then use `jq -Rs` to inject it as the `body` field:
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0984647Z ```bash
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0984916Z cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/gh-aw/body.md
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0985226Z Title
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0985367Z 
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0985493Z Multi-line body content goes here.
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0985802Z EOF
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0986202Z jq -Rs '{title: "My title", body: .}' /tmp/gh-aw/body.md | safeoutputs create_discussion .
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0986661Z ```
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0987395Z If a shell command is rejected for containing expansion patterns, do not retry the same command — switch to the heredoc + `jq -Rs` pattern above.
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0987969Z 
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0988355Z To inject an entire local file as the `body` field without re-embedding its content in the model context, use `jq -Rs`:
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0988946Z ```bash
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0989251Z jq -Rs --arg discussion_number "$DISCUSSION_NUMBER" \
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0989968Z   '{discussion_number: ($discussion_number|tonumber), body: .}' \
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0991276Z   discussion-body.md \
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0991664Z   | safeoutputs update_discussion .
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0991993Z ```
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0992833Z `jq -Rs` reads the file as a raw string (`-R`) and slurps it into a single JSON string value (`-s`), so `body` is always a valid JSON field. Piping `cat file | safeoutputs ...` does not populate `body` and will be rejected.
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0993604Z 
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0994131Z The generated command syntax above is schema-derived from each enabled tool's final `inputSchema` and is the source of truth for required/optional parameters.
2026-09-22T10:02:38.0995340Z Use `<server> --help` and `<server> <tool> --help` for the same schema-derived signatures and examples before calling any command.

2026-09-22T10:02:38.1012095Z non-command work, do not sweep the repo). If BOTH are empty, run
2026-09-22T10:02:38.1012611Z Non-Command Mode. (Two separate expressions on purpose: gh-aw's

2026-09-22T10:02:38.1013926Z defined-but-empty env — never rejoin them.) Use the deterministic scripts (`docs/repo-assist.md` has the table):
